label: Demand rises and supply falls with height together, so the flyable heights reach down to the ground
statement_en: In an atmosphere where air density and oxygen partial pressure both fall with height, the minimum speed of lift-supported flight and the power to fly at it are nondecreasing in height, while the aerobic supply (with arterial content nondecreasing in partial pressure, as a Hill curve gives) is nonincreasing. Hence sustained flight possible at a height is possible at every lower height; above an infeasible height every height is infeasible, so the flyable set is an interval from the ground up to a ceiling; and a design that cannot fly at the ground cannot fly at any height. A larger lifting area lowers the power required at a fixed height.

kernelChecked: That the minimum speed and the power required at it are nondecreasing in height, given only that air density falls with height.
That the aerobic supply is nonincreasing in height, given only that oxygen partial pressure falls with height and arterial content is nondecreasing in it.
That the feasible heights are downward closed, that infeasibility propagates upward (a ceiling in that sense), and that infeasibility at the ground forces infeasibility everywhere.
That a larger lifting area lowers the power required at a fixed height.

lean.source:
/-- **The feasible heights reach down to the ground.** If the design can fly at a height, it can fly at
every lower one: demand only falls as you descend and supply only rises. -/
theorem feasible_downward_closed {ca : ℝ → ℝ} (hca : ∀ x y : ℝ, x ≤ y → ca x ≤ ca y)
    {W S CL LD eta E Q : ℝ} (hW : 0 < W) (hS : 0 < S) (hCL : 0 < CL) (hLD : 0 < LD)
    (he : 0 ≤ eta) (hE : 0 ≤ E) (hQ : 0 ≤ Q) {h₁ h₂ : ℝ} (hle : h₁ ≤ h₂)
    (hfeas : Feasible A ca W S CL LD eta E Q h₂) : Feasible A ca W S CL LD eta E Q h₁ := by
  unfold Feasible at hfeas ⊢
  calc demandAt A W S CL LD h₁ ≤ demandAt A W S CL LD h₂ := demand_mono A hW hS hCL hLD hle
    _ ≤ supplyAt A ca eta E Q h₂ := hfeas
    _ ≤ supplyAt A ca eta E Q h₁ := supply_anti A hca he hE hQ hle

named_hypotheses.name: Delphi.Altitude.Feasible
named_hypotheses.source:
/-- Sustained flight is possible at height `h` when the aerobic supply there covers the power required
there. "Feasible" in the model's sense only: it says the oxygen budget is not what forbids the flight, and
nothing about burst power, structure, control, heat or whether the animal exists. -/
def Feasible (ca : ℝ → ℝ) (W S CL LD eta E Q h : ℝ) : Prop :=
  demandAt A W S CL LD h ≤ supplyAt A ca eta E Q h
